facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with new and progressive satellite lesions while undergoing pembrolizumab therapy
Two years earlier, he had undergone a wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
An incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved, with no evidence of distant metastatic disease
Multiple unresectable satellite lesions appeared
He received 4 cycles of ipilimumab, followed by a second wide local excision when new lesions appeared
Additional satellite lesions developed and he began pembrolizumab therapy, but after 5 cycles, local progression occurred in the satellite lesions
Multiple satellite lesions were present on the left posterior auricular scalp area
clinically regressed lesions with persistent black pigmentation were noted
H&E sections showed intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, histiocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
SOX-10 and MART-1: Highlighted normal melanocytes in basal layer of epidermis only
CD163 and myeloperoxidase: Highlighted histiocytes and neutrophils respectively
complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation; MART-1 immunostain confirms complete tumor regression

concepts.why: The patient's history of a left posterior auricular scalp lesion, incidentally resected lymph node with focal involvement, and multiple satellite lesions, along with histopathology findings of intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate and immunostaining results, support the diagnosis of melanoma.

The patient's history of multiple unresectable satellite lesions, local progression after pembrolizumab therapy, and clinically regressed lesions with persistent black pigmentation, support the diagnosis of recurrent melanoma.

The patient's history of a resected lymph node with focal involvement and local progression after pembrolizumab therapy, along with histopathology findings, support the diagnosis of metastatic melanoma.
The patient's history of multiple satellite lesions with persistent black pigmentation, along with immunostaining results highlighting normal melanocytes, support the diagnosis of pigmented melanoma.
The patient's histopathology findings of intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate and immunostaining results highlighting histiocytes and neutrophils, support the diagnosis of inflammatory melanoma.

rationales.F01: New and progressive satellite lesions suggest recurrent melanoma
rationales.F03: Incidentally resected lymph node with focal involvement indicates potential for metastasis
rationales.F07: Multiple satellite lesions on the left posterior auricular scalp area are consistent with recurrent melanoma
rationales.F09: Intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate is consistent with inflammatory melanoma
rationales.F12: Complete tumor regression and neutrophil-rich mixed inflammation suggest a positive response to treatment

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of multiple unresectable satellite lesions, local progression despite pembrolizumab therapy, and previous wide local excision with graft repair supports the diagnosis of Recurrent Melanoma, which is a more specific entity than Melanoma.
